title: Breathless woman with a racing pulse
stem: A 38 year old woman presents with six months of worsening breathlessness on exertion, orthopnoea and palpitations. She had rheumatic fever as a child. Her pulse feels irregular.

history.q: How far can you walk before you stop?
history.a: She stops after about 100 metres on the flat and must rest on stairs.

history.q: Do you wake breathless at night?
history.a: Yes, twice a week she wakes gasping and sits upright for relief.

history.q: Any chest pain, cough or fever?
history.a: No chest pain. Occasional dry cough, no fever, no haemoptysis.
Rheumatic fever at age 11. No regular medicines. No known drug allergies.

exam.general: Comfortable at rest, mild malar flush, no ankle oedema.
exam.pulse: Irregularly irregular pulse at 92 per minute, normal volume and character.
exam.jvp: Jugular venous pressure not raised, no prominent waves.
exam.precordium: Tapping apex beat in the fifth intercostal space at the midclavicular line.

auscultation.s2: Normally split second heart sound with an opening snap shortly after
auscultation.murmur: Low pitched rumbling mid diastolic murmur at the apex, grade 3 of 4, no radiation, best heard with the bell in the left lateral position

findings: No P waves with an irregularly irregular ventricular response

echoTasks.find: Enlarged left atrium and a thickened doming mitral valve with restricted opening
Thickened mitral leaflets with doming of the anterior leaflet in diastole

diagnosis.answer: Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with atrial fibrillation
accept: severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with atrial fibrillation
severe mitral stenosis with atrial fibrillation

management.model: Rate control for atrial fibrillation, anticoagulation for mitral stenosis with atrial fibrillation, diuretics for congestion, and referral for mitral balloon valvuloplasty assessment at a tertiary centre. Rheumatic fever secondary prophylaxis is reviewed.
keyPoints: Anticoagulate for atrial fibrillation with rheumatic mitral stenosis
Refer for balloon mitral valvuloplasty assessment

teaching: A loud first sound, an opening snap and a rumbling mid diastolic murmur point to mitral stenosis.
Left atrial enlargement predisposes to atrial fibrillation.
sources: ASE guidance on valvular stenosis, restated in own words
